title: Ukrainian garrison leaves Azovstal steelworks in Mariupol
body:
On 16 May 2022, more than 260 Ukrainian fighters, some seriously wounded, left the Azovstal steel plant in Mariupol and turned themselves over to Russian forces under a negotiated deal. More than 50 were seriously wounded, according to both sides. On 17 May seven more buses carrying an unknown number of soldiers arrived at a former penal colony in Olenivka, about 88 kilometres north of Mariupol. The plant covers about 11 square kilometres.

Russia called the event a surrender. Ukraine avoided that word and said the garrison had completed its mission of tying down Russian forces. Defense Minister Oleksiy Reznikov said the priority was to save the fighters' lives. Russian parliament speaker Vyacheslav Volodin claimed, without evidence, that there were "war criminals" among the defenders and said they should be tried rather than exchanged. Russia's top prosecutor asked the Supreme Court to designate Ukraine's Azov Regiment a terrorist organisation.

Ukraine said Russian bombardment had killed more than 20,000 civilians in Mariupol, which had a prewar population of 430,000. Full control of the city would give Russia an unbroken land bridge to Crimea. The Associated Press reported that it was impossible to confirm the total number of fighters or their legal status, and that the International Criminal Court's chief prosecutor had sent a team of 42 investigators to Ukraine.
